TRIAGE OF ALEX'S 2026-08-30 FIELD REPORT (grok-shell-reflow2 1.0.13, running reflow2 0.43.0), relayed by Anthony. Two files were handed over; ONE WAS ALREADY CAPTURED and is recorded here so nobody re-triages it.

═══ WHICH FILE IS WHICH, READ OFF THE FILES ═══
The 08-29 upload is the SAME report already committed as docs/feedback/2026-08-29-grok-shell-agent-feedback.md — differently formatted, same two items, no new information. The 08-30 upload is NEW: items 1 and 2 still reproduced on 0.43.0, plus four previously unreported. Registered as art:grok-shell-feedback-2026-08-30.

═══ ① HIS ITEM 2 IS ALREADY FIXED, AND HE IS ON THE WRONG VERSION ═══
He asks: *"name the TYPE in the refusal so the agent knows it is looking at a different kind of node."* v0.44.0 does exactly that — crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/capture.rs:594 emits *"The design already holds a DIFFERENT KIND OF RECORD saying something close to this"* and names the type.

VERIFIED BY USE, not by reading the code: this session hit that refusal THREE TIMES on 0.44.0 and it named the near-match as a Decision and as a DesignEpoch each time. Alex is running 0.43.0. **The fix shipped and did not reach the user who asked for it**, which is a distribution finding rather than a design one.

═══ ② HIS ITEM 1 IS NOW ON ITS THIRD INDEPENDENT REPORT ═══
  2026-08-27  Grok Build TUI      art:grok-build-tui-feedback-2026-08-27
  2026-08-29  grok-shell 1.0.13   art:grok-shell-feedback-2026-08-29
  2026-08-30  grok-shell 1.0.13   art:grok-shell-feedback-2026-08-30

Three sessions, two different clients, same symptom: every non-prose non-refusal reply is a stub, so `search_design`, `get_node`, `loop_status`, `detect_gaps` and every `add_*` success is invisible. HE RANKS IT HIS OWN #1 and says everything else is downstream of it. His whole session ran on `export_graph` to a scratch path plus a JSON parse — a full-graph dump to answer *"did this one write stick?"*

The design already holds this as `dec:idea-how-does-a-content-only-client-get-an-answer` (OPEN) and knows why the duplication was removed (`fact:every-reply-was-sent-twice`, `ver:a-reply-is-sent-once`). What is new is the third occurrence and his priority ordering.

⭐ AND IT IS THE EXPERIMENT v0.44.0 EXISTS FOR. `fact:reflow2-sends-a-structured-payload-for-tools-that-declare-no-output-contract` (2026-08-29) set up a control arm: one tool declares an output contract, the rest do not, and a user calls both in one session. ALEX ON 0.44.0 IS THAT EXPERIMENT, and his report is the pre-condition measurement on 0.43.0 — 'neither arrives' — taken without anyone asking for it.

═══ ③ NEW AND ACTIONABLE: A DEPENDENT WRITE IN A PARALLEL BATCH FAILS, AND THE FAILURE IS INVISIBLE ═══
His item 3. A harness emitted `add_change_event` and `pin_at_epoch` naming that same ChangeEvent IN ONE PARALLEL BATCH. The pin lost the race and refused with *"Node not found"*. Then `set_artifact_checksum` with `design_change_event_id` pointing at it returned only the stub, and the next export still carried the OLD checksum — so the write had failed and nothing said so.

🛑 THE SHARP EDGE IS THE COMBINATION, NOT EITHER HALF. A racing write is recoverable if you can see it fail; an invisible success is survivable if writes do not race. Together they produce a COMMITTED EXPORT WHOSE ARTIFACT HASHES DO NOT MATCH DISK, which is the state the drift gate exists to prevent. This session avoided it only by sequencing the same three calls by hand.

His own suggestion, worth taking on its merits: a line in the pin/checksum refusal saying "create the ChangeEvent first", and serialising writes that name a just-created id.

═══ ④ ITEMS 4 AND 5 ARE DOCUMENTATION, AND HE LABELS THEM SO ═══
`get_instructions {section: "existing-design"}` — a slug guessed from prose that does not exist; and `get_skill {name: "where"}` — the slash command is `where`, the served skill is `where-am-i`. BOTH REFUSALS WERE CORRECT AND ACTIONABLE and he says so. Item 6 is item 1's consequence, not a separate finding.

═══ WHAT HE SAYS WORKS, RECORDED BECAUSE PRAISE IS EVIDENCE TOO ═══
Refusals arrive complete and actionable in `content`; the four prose tools return whole documents; sectioned `get_instructions` avoids the ~27 KB cap; `export_graph` with a path is a reliable read/write; `distinct_from` unblocks cross-type matches once treated as normal.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether item 1 is a reflow2 defect or a grok-shell-reflow2 1.0.13 conformance gap. He says he cannot tell, and neither can this session — reflow2 made a deliberate trade (stop duplicating, because duplication was the difference between a readable reply and a refused one) and that trade breaks this client. Naming it a client bug would be convenient and is not established.
